result_text:
**Enterprise revenue for 2026 Q2 (April through June) was $925,797.78, from 199 orders.**

By month it was $300,965.51 in April, $301,056.40 in May and $323,775.87 in June.

This was a bounded lookup that the ledger settles, so I didn't run a hypothesis loop. I did check the join before trusting it.

- **Duplicate account rows:** `accounts.csv` has 70 rows for 60 accounts. Nine accounts appear more than once because their region or owner changed, and one of them (A1010) appears three times.
- **Segment stability:** No account ever changes segment, so each account maps to exactly one segment. That makes the segment assignment unambiguous regardless of order date.
- **Fan-out avoided:** I mapped each account to its single segment before joining. A naive join on `account_id` would have counted orders on the duplicated accounts more than once and given $1,227,245.07 for Enterprise, an overstatement of about $301K.
- **Reconciliation:** The Enterprise, Mid-Market ($542,840.57) and SMB ($223,120.39) figures sum to $1,691,758.74. That equals the total of all 1,050 Q2 orders.
- **Data checks:** Every order's `account_id` exists in the accounts file. Order IDs are unique, all amounts are positive, and the ledger covers 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30.

"Revenue" here means the sum of `amount_usd` on orders dated in the quarter. The file has no refund, credit or cancellation fields, so the figure is gross order value.

The calculation output is saved at `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s22c-pre-h4sdx7xq/work/enterprise_q2_2026.txt`.
